key_insight: A phononic subsurface embedded in a flat plate can systematically reshape sustained vortex shedding, with its chordwise position and resonant growth rate controlling whether lift/drag oscillations are amplified or strongly damped.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a passive flow-control strategy for reducing unsteady loads in separated-flow systems while preserving mean aerodynamic performance.
method: High-fidelity immersed boundary FSI simulations of fully separated flow over a flat plate with an embedded grounded diatomic-chain phononic subsurface.
Swept two controls: chordwise placement of the subsurface and the growth rate of its resonant displacement envelope.
Analyzed limit-cycle behavior, characteristic frequencies, phase between subsurface motion and lift, and unsteady/mean flow fields.
evidence_signal: The simulations identified four position-dependent regimes, including a configuration that reduced lift oscillation amplitude by over 30% and drag oscillation amplitude by over 50% with less than 0.5% change in mean lift and drag.
watch_item: The reported benefits are highly configuration-dependent, so practical implementation will require careful tuning of subsurface placement and resonant response to match the target separated flow.
paper_title: Interaction of Sustained Vortex Shedding with a Phononic Subsurface: Effect of Positioning and Resonant Characteristics
